title: Bounded column mixtures can hide higher dust opacity indices over finite wavelength ranges
abstract: We test whether dip spectra can identify a power law dust opacity index when the column distribution is free. Positive stable Laplace transforms show that every spectrum from index b can also come from any higher index B in a pure foreground screen with common stellar surface color. Exact representations can have infinite mean column. We prove that capping columns at T reduces the error to at most C exp(-k_min T), so bounded columns with finite mean can reproduce the spectrum to any finite precision on a finite wavelength range. For a uniform index-0.25 screen that fits the main published TIC 300651846 dip, an index-1 mixture with reference optical depth at most 23.583 matches its whole 0.4-5 micrometer spectrum to a proved 10 ppm bound. The largest sampled difference is 0.660 ppm. We also derive a spectral slope bound when an independent column cap exists. This is a conditional method and identifiability result, not a new dust measurement. Unknown surface color, real opacity features, emission, and independent mass or column constraints limit its use. Code, proofs, source hashes, synthetic predictions, and repeat steps are included. External source tables are not bundled.

display.caption: A shallow opacity law and a steeper law with bounded column mixtures give nearly equal spectra. The two observed depths calibrate the shallow screen; all curves are model predictions.
